subject: Agriculture
title: Norman Borlaug's Mission
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Norman Borlaug's Mission.

hook.text: Norman Borlaug, an Iowa farm boy, spent decades breeding wheat in Mexico. He saved a billion lives.

buildup.text: In the 1940s, the Rockefeller Foundation sent Borlaug to Mexico to fight wheat rust disease.

discovery.text: Borlaug crossed thousands of wheat varieties, selecting for disease resistance and high yield simultaneously.

twist.text: Mexican farmers initially rejected his new seeds. He had to prove them in the field, row by painful row.

climax.text: By 1963, Mexico went from wheat importer to wheat exporter. Borlaug's varieties changed a nation.

punchline.text: One scientist, one crop, a billion people fed.

quiz.question: What crop did Norman Borlaug spend decades improving?

details.summary: Norman Borlaug was an American agronomist who developed high-yielding, disease-resistant wheat varieties that saved an estimated one billion people from starvation. Known as the father of the Green Revolution, he won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for his contributions to world food supply.
details.whyItMatters: Borlaug is credited with saving more lives than any other person in history. His work proved that agricultural science could solve seemingly intractable food crises and inspired generations of crop scientists.
takeaways: Borlaug developed dwarf wheat varieties that doubled and tripled yields in Mexico and Asia
His work is credited with saving an estimated one billion people from starvation
He is one of only seven people to win the Nobel Peace Prize, Presidential Medal of Freedom, and Congressional Gold Medal

faq.question: How did Norman Borlaug's wheat varieties save so many lives?
faq.answer: Borlaug bred semi-dwarf wheat that could absorb high doses of fertilizer without falling over (lodging). These varieties yielded 2-3 times more grain per acre. When introduced to India and Pakistan in the mid-1960s, they averted predicted famines and transformed both countries into wheat exporters.

faq.question: What personal qualities drove Borlaug's success?
faq.answer: Borlaug combined scientific brilliance with extraordinary determination. He worked in Mexican fields for 20 years before achieving recognition. He personally lobbied skeptical governments to adopt his varieties. He famously said, 'You can't build a peaceful world on empty stomachs.'
